name: Josheb-basshebeth
overview: Josheb-basshebeth was a male warrior from the tribe of Judah, distinguished as the first of "the thirty" mighty men who served King David. He was identified as a Tahchemonite or Hachmonite, indicating his specific clan or family group. Josheb-basshebeth held a significant military role, having charge of the first division for the first month in David's organized army.
namesAndTitles: Josheb-basshebeth means "one sitting in the seat," which may imply a position of authority or honor. He is also known by the names Adino the Eznite and Jashobeam, the latter meaning "the people return." These names reflect different traditions or textual variants but consistently identify the same individual.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Josheb-basshebeth was the father of Zabdiel, as noted in the organization of David's army. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Josheb-basshebeth's prominence as the foremost among David's elite warriors highlights his importance in the establishment and defense of David's kingdom. His leadership of the first military division underscores his trusted role in the king's army. The multiple names attributed to him across different scriptural books emphasize his recognized status among David's mighty men.
